This occurs despite Nvidia stating US export controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-center market. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 14, 2026 at 05:00 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * A Reuters review found over $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects using Nvidia's restricted chips. * Projects span from coastal tech hubs to western provinces, showing Nvidia's deep market integration. * Key projects specify Nvidia H100 and H200 chips for large-scale AI development. * Existing facilities in Jiangsu and Fujian are already operating with Nvidia H800 processors. A Reuters review has identified over $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia)'s restricted processors. This development comes even as Nvidia has stated that US [export controls](/tag/export+controls) have effectively excluded it from [China](/tag/china)'s AI data-centre market. These projects span from China's wealthy coastal technology hubs to its remote western provinces. This underscores how deeply Nvidia's technology remains integrated into China's AI expansion. ### Key Projects and Deployments A proposed 6.2 billion yuan ($873 million) AI computing centre in Fujian province, specifically Xianyou county, is seeking commercial partners. This facility specifies Nvidia [H100](/tag/h100) chips for large-scale AI development. In Shaanxi province, state-owned engineering group Sinomach reported that a subsidiary secured a contract for a 3 billion yuan computing centre. This project specifies Nvidia H100 and [H200](/tag/h200) processors. Jilin province has an April government prospectus detailing a 2.26 billion yuan project. This combines Nvidia H100 processors with Chinese-developed chips, with developers expecting bank loans for 80 per cent of the investment. Inner Mongolia is planning a 1.5 billion-yuan development that proposes installing 625 Nvidia H200 servers. Chinese industry reports in June indicated that construction had commenced on two buildings in its initial phase. These plans highlight developers' continued reliance on US processors, which are vulnerable to trade restrictions. Tighter curbs risk construction delays, inflated costs, or forced redesigns using domestic alternatives. In Gansu province, a local company was awarded a 1.16 billion yuan construction contract in July for a computing centre. This facility plans to install approximately 3,072 Nvidia processors, with tender documents specifying H100 and H200 hardware. The contract went to a consortium led by a subsidiary of state-owned Shaanxi Construction Engineering; however, the documents do not confirm processor delivery. Other Chinese facilities are already utilising restricted Nvidia hardware. The Wuxi municipal government in Jiangsu province stated in March 2025 that a computing cluster using Nvidia [H800](/tag/h800) processors had become operational. In Fujian, Shanghai-listed Damingcheng disclosed in June that a computing venture had built an H800 cluster, signing a 759 million yuan computing-services agreement that concluded early. Smaller purchases also indicate sustained demand from research institutions. Shenzhen University secured a contract for three H100 processors in September. others are in Shaanxi, Jilin, Inner Mongolia, Gansu, Wuxi and Fujian [[2]](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/chinas-3-billionplus-pipeline-of-nvidiapowered-ai-data-centres-5024599). * Reuters said the projects have not been linked to Megaspeed or the allegations involving Alice Huang, and that it did not establish how the restricted hardware reached Chinese buyers [[1]](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivehuang-exit-and-us-scrutiny-imperil-3-billion-in-chinese-ai-projects-reliant-on-nvidia-5024462). * Hong Kong-listed AI developers fell again on Friday: Z.AI dropped 7.4%, MiniMax 4.9% and Tencent 2.6% in morning trading [[3]](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/asia-stocks-steady-chipmakers-rebound-042520486.html). ![Huang's exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion of Chinese AI data centers built on Nvidia chips, Reuters reports](/media/news_images/huangs-exit-and-us-scrutiny-imperil-3-billion-of-chinese-ai-data-centers-built-o.jpg) More than $3 billion of Chinese AI data center projects designed around [Nvidia](/companies/nvidia/) processors that the US bars from export to China are at risk of delays, supply disruption or costly redesigns as Washington weighs tighter controls after [Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive](/news/jensen-huang-resigns-as-nvidia-ceo-cfo-colette-kress-named-interim-chief-executive/), Reuters reported on Friday [[1]](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivehuang-exit-and-us-scrutiny-imperil-3-billion-in-chinese-ai-projects-reliant-on-nvidia-5024462). Nebius led the decline, dropping about 9.6% to roughly $115.77 after guiding 2026 revenue to the low end of its range. Nvidia shares fell as much as 12% before paring losses to about 7.5%. The sell-off spread across semiconductors, with Marvell, Oracle and Micron lower, while AMD and Broadcom gained on expectations that Nvidia's turmoil could benefit rivals. The Dow, Nasdaq and S&P 500 all closed modestly lower. ##### Key Elements ![Nvidia CEO Exit Sparks AI Data Center Rout as CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN Plunge](https://img.biggo.com/uCaipe4__3vFwC_hM21nvFAYOW1lCKtS4ohg2ug7fbk/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzkxN2Y3ZTlmLTc4YWEtNGM2Ni1iNDEyLTQ4ZGQxMTA0MWQxYl8xNzk0NTkyNjc4X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Shares of AI-focused data center operators sold off sharply on Friday after Nvidia's abrupt leadership change raised questions about whether the chipmaker will keep bankrolling the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure. CoreWeave (CRWV) fell about 8%, Nebius (NBIS) dropped roughly 9.6% and IREN Limited (IREN) slid 8.1% in afternoon trading, according to TipRanks data. Nebius led the group lower, trading near $115.77, after the company said 2026 revenue would land at the bottom of its previously guided range, according to Reuters. The trigger was Nvidia (NVDA), where longtime chief executive Jensen Huang was forced out on Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs. Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer, took over as interim CEO. Investors latched onto a Reuters report that Kress, months before Huang's departure, had pushed back on his riskier spending plans. Those included a proposed $250 billion investment in an OpenAI data center in Ohio, as well as aggressive bets on AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda. Nvidia shares themselves fell as much as 12% early in the session before paring losses to about 7.5%, a swing that at one point threatened to erase more than $500 billion in market value, Reuters reported. The neocloud operators — so named because they rent out GPU capacity rather than owning the underlying chips — are among the most exposed names in the AI trade. Nvidia has supplied capital and hardware to several of them, a practice that has drawn scrutiny over the circular nature of AI financing. "Nvidia has been called the 'bank of AI,'" said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading. "If this situation forces them to step back from funding, will the supply to smaller companies that need capital be cut off? We don't know the answer yet." The selling spread across the semiconductor complex. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 1.3%. Marvell Technology (MRVL), which Huang in June called "the next trillion-dollar company," fell 3.8%, while Oracle (ORCL), a major cloud provider expanding its AI chip business with Nvidia, slipped 2.6%. Memory maker Micron Technology (MU) declined 2.5%, and data storage companies SanDisk (SNDK) and Western Digital (WDC) dropped 6% and 3.7%, respectively. Optical component makers Lumentum (LITE) and Coherent (COHR) and AI server maker Dell (DELL) each fell between 3% and 5.1%. Industrial bellwethers Caterpillar (CAT) and utility Vistra (VST) edged down about 0.5%. Not every chip name suffered. Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # Chinese AI firms secure Nvidia chip capacity abroad amid US curbs fears Chinese artificial intelligence companies are seeking to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centres outside China. This move is driven by concerns that a scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could lead to tighter US restrictions on remote AI chip access. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 13, 2026 at 11:20 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * Chinese AI firms are renting Nvidia-powered computing capacity at overseas data centres. * Concerns over a Jensen Huang scandal could tighten US remote chip access restrictions. * Proposed US Remote Access Security Act (RASA) would regulate cloud access to restricted tech. * Increased demand for Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market fuels stockpiling by traders. Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies are attempting to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centres located outside China, according to three people familiar with the matter. This action stems from concerns that a controversy involving [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia)'s chief executive, Jensen Huang, could prompt Washington to tighten restrictions on remote access to advanced processors. US [export controls](/tag/export+controls) currently limit the direct export of Nvidia's most advanced [AI chips](/tag/ai+chips) to China. However, Chinese firms can bypass these restrictions by renting computing power from overseas data centres that utilise such processors. A major Chinese cloud provider has discussed internally securing overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have contacted data centre operators for reservations. Smaller AI labs are also exploring similar steps, including approaching major providers in Southeast Asia, two of the people said. These companies reportedly fear that the controversy surrounding Huang could add political momentum to the [Remote Access Security Act](/tag/remote+access+security+act) (RASA). This proposed US bill would grant the Commerce Department authority to regulate cloud-based access to restricted technology. The House of Representatives passed RASA in January, and it awaits Senate action. Advanced Nvidia processors are crucial for training and running large AI models that power chatbots and other [generative AI](/tag/generative+ai) products. Restricting overseas cloud access would make it more difficult for Chinese developers to obtain high-end computing power without direct chip imports. ### Market and Enforcement Concerns The prospect of tougher enforcement has also increased demand for restricted Nvidia AI chips in China's grey market. Traders and intermediaries have begun stockpiling these processors, two of the sources stated. Buyers fear the controversy could lead to a broader US crackdown on smuggling advanced chips and AI servers into China. Procurement records indicate that a Chinese university, despite being on a US export blacklist, purchased Nvidia H200 AI chips last month. This highlights existing gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology. US prosecutors in March charged Super Micro Computer co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two others with conspiring to divert servers containing Nvidia chips to China. This was allegedly done through a Southeast Asia-based company that bought approximately $2.5 billion of servers from Super Micro between 2024 and 2025. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?
